project.objective: Besides their children John, Hannah Grace, Edwin, William, and James, did Hannah Earnest and Edwin Grice have any other children? Identify each additional child and their birth details.

questions.question: Did Hannah Earnest (born 1857, Darlaston, Staffordshire) and Edwin Grice (born 1854, West Bromwich, Staffordshire) have any children besides John, Hannah Grace, Edwin, William, and James Grice, and if so, who were those children and what were their birth details?
questions.rationale: The objective is a family-completeness question covering roughly 1876–1891 (the span implied by the known children's births) in Staffordshire and Warwickshire, England. Census records for 1881 and 1891 already appear in the tree's sources and list household members; baptism/christening registers and civil registration birth indexes for West Bromwich, Darlaston, and Birmingham survive well for this period and would capture any additional births. A systematic search of these records can either surface additional children or support a negative conclusion. No questions yet exist, so this first question restates the objective with identifying detail as required.

items.jurisdiction: West Bromwich, Staffordshire, England, United Kingdom
items.rationale: The 1881 census (FamilySearch collection 2562194, name-searchable) lists every person in each household on 3 April 1881. Search for Edwin Grice as head of household in West Bromwich and Darlaston. All children resident on census night appear by name and age. The known children span c.1877–1886, so this census captures those born by early 1881 and still living. Any additional child born before April 1881 and alive on that date would appear here. Priority 1 because it is free, indexed, and directly enumerates the household.

items.jurisdiction: West Bromwich, Staffordshire, England, United Kingdom
items.rationale: The 1891 census (FamilySearch collection 1865747, name-searchable) lists the household on 5 April 1891. By this date all five known children would be between approximately 5 and 14 years old if still living. Any additional child born between 1881 and 1891 and surviving to that date would appear here. Comparing the 1881 and 1891 household rosters reveals children who appeared in one census but not the other — evidence of a birth and death between enumeration years. Search Edwin Grice as head in West Bromwich and Darlaston.

items.jurisdiction: West Bromwich, Staffordshire, England, United Kingdom
items.rationale: The 1901 census (FamilySearch collection 1888129, name-searchable) lists the household on 31 March 1901. Older children may have left home by this date; youngest children born in the 1890s would still be resident. Cross-referencing all three census households (1881, 1891, 1901) provides a near-complete picture of children who survived to at least one enumeration year. Children appearing in 1901 but absent from both earlier censuses would indicate a birth in the 1891–1901 window.

Church christening search (England, Births and Christenings 1538-1975, collection 1473014) for father Edwin Grice in West Bromwich returned 101 results. Key records: Hannah Grace christened 5 May 1880 (father Edwin Grace/Grice, mother Hannah — confirmed); Fanny Grise christened 6 Mar 1889 (father Edwin Grise/Grice, mother indexed as Anne — suspect transcription of Hannah, flagged for image confirmation); James Grice christened 27 Oct 1886 (father Edwin Grice confirmed). Extraction in progress.

Staffordshire, England, Church of England Births and Baptisms, 1813–1900 (Ancestry collection 62292, name-searchable) and England & Wales Non-Conformist Registers, 1567–1936 (Ancestry dbid=2972). Per loc_001, Darlaston had four Wesleyan Methodist places of worship; a child not found in Anglican registers may have been baptised in a Nonconformist chapel. The Nonconformist registers are held at The National Archives and indexed on Ancestry. This item is a fallback for pli_008 and also covers the Nonconformist gap that the FamilySearch Anglican search cannot address. Findmypast Staffordshire Baptisms, 1538–1900 is an additional alternative index.

British Newspaper Archive / Findmypast Staffordshire newspaper titles including the County Advertiser & Herald for Staffordshire and Worcestershire (1856–1907) and the Darlaston Weekly Times (1882–1887, Findmypast). Per loc_001, these papers may carry birth, death, and infant death notices for the Grice family. A birth announcement or mourning notice for an infant child may be the only surviving record of a child who died before civil registration was completed or before any census year. Particularly valuable for the 1882–1887 window when the Darlaston Weekly Times was in print.

quirks: Darlaston births are registered under the Walsall civil registration district (not West Bromwich). Always search the Walsall district GRO index for Darlaston events.
West Bromwich births are registered under the West Bromwich civil registration district. A family moving between the two towns will have children registered in different districts.
Darlaston All Saints chapelry was created in 1872 from the ancient Darlaston St Lawrence parish. Post-1872 baptisms may appear in either register; search both.
GRO indexes are filed by the quarter of registration, not the date of birth. A birth on 20 March registered on 6 April appears in the April-June quarter.
It was common English practice to reuse a child's Christian name if the first child with that name died in infancy. Search burial registers alongside baptism registers for the same given name.

The GRO website (gro.gov.uk) provides the mother's maiden name on birth index searches for free — most third-party sites do not show this for pre-1911 records. Use the GRO site to confirm a match belongs to the right family.

The 1911 census (just outside the target period) asks the wife for total children born alive, still living, and deceased — a direct count that can surface all births including those that left no other surviving record.
Darlaston had four Wesleyan places of worship. Search Nonconformist registers (held at The National Archives and on Ancestry/FamilySearch) if a child is not found in Anglican registers.

Records from this period are in Staffordshire Record Office (pre-1974). Post-1974 the area became West Midlands; Sandwell Archives holds some later local authority records but not the historical registers.
Neighbouring parishes include Wednesbury and Walsall. A child baptised near a parish boundary may appear in a neighbouring register; search these if not found in Darlaston or West Bromwich registers.
The Darlaston Weekly Times (1882-1887) at Findmypast may carry infant death or birth notices for children who do not survive to census years.
Staffordshire Name Indexes (staffsnameindexes.org.uk) is a locally-maintained volunteer index worth consulting alongside national databases.
localities.guide_markdown:
# Locality Guide: West Bromwich and Darlaston, Staffordshire, England (1875–1900)

## Jurisdiction overview

- West Bromwich is an ancient parish and civil registration district in the South Offlow hundred of Staffordshire. The civil registration district of West Bromwich was created in 1837. In 1974 the area transferred to West Midlands.
- Darlaston is an ancient parish (records from 1539) in the South Offlow hundred. Its civil registration district is Walsall — not West Bromwich.
- County archive: Staffordshire Record Office. Ecclesiastical diocese: Lichfield, Province of Canterbury.
- Economy: Iron and steel manufacturing, bolt and nut making, coal mining (Black Country).
- Religious denominations: Church of England; strong Wesleyan Methodist presence (four Wesleyan places of worship in Darlaston); Baptist; Roman Catholic (Birmingham Archdiocese).

## Boundary changes

- Both towns in Staffordshire throughout 1875–1900; transferred to West Midlands in 1974.
- Critical registration split: West Bromwich births filed under West Bromwich district; Darlaston births filed under Walsall district. Search both.
- Darlaston All Saints chapelry established 1872 from ancient St Lawrence parish; post-1872 baptisms may appear in either register.

## Available record types

### Vital records (civil registration)

- National civil registration began 1 July 1837 (England_Civil_Registration wiki). Mandatory with penalties from 1875 onward; coverage 1875–1900 is essentially complete.
- Registration districts: West Bromwich → West Bromwich district; Darlaston → Walsall district.
- Free access: FreeBMD (freebmd.org.uk), GRO website (gro.gov.uk), FamilySearch collection 2285338.
- Subscription: Ancestry collection 8912 (births 1837–1915); Findmypast; Staffordshire BMD indexes (Ancestry collection 61709).
- GRO certificates must be ordered from GRO; index alone is freely searchable.

### Church records

- Darlaston St Lawrence: registers from 1539; Bishop's Transcripts from 1660.
- Darlaston All Saints (chapelry): established 1872.
- West Bromwich All Saints: registers from 1608; chapelries St Paul (1853) and St Peter (1858).
- West Bromwich Christ Church: registers from 1829.
- West Bromwich Holy Trinity: registers from 1841.
- FamilySearch digitized Darlaston church records (32 volumes total, first page returned): key volumes covering 1875–1900 are 100885191 (All Saints baptisms 1891–1905, 100% indexed), 102021571 (1854–1900, 100% indexed), 102021572 (1885–1898, 100% indexed), 102021568 (1883–1891, 100% indexed), 102021569 (1891–1899, 100% indexed).
- Pre-1886 Darlaston baptism microfilm volumes (007566563/007566564 series): 0 images online; physical microfilm only.
- Staffordshire-wide: FamilySearch collection 2364451 (1538–1944, indexed + images); Ancestry collection 62292 (baptisms 1813–1900); Findmypast Staffordshire Baptisms.

### Census records

- 1881 (April 3), 1891 (April 5), 1901 (March 31) — all indexed + images online, free at FamilySearch.
- No state or off-year census for England.
- 1911 census (FamilySearch collection 1921547) asks wife for total children born, living, and deceased — critical for family completeness.

### Cemetery records

- James Bridge Cemetery, Darlaston (opened 1860): burial registers 1860–1908 digitized at FamilySearch (full-text searchable, 0% name-indexed — must browse image by image).
- Cemetery records 1860–1991 and 1888–1970: multiple FamilySearch volumes, full-text searchable, 0% name-indexed.
- Burial register index 1860–1976 available (volume 008072650_010, 68 images).
- Monumental Inscriptions of St Lawrence, Darlaston and Wesleyan Methodist Church, Pinfold Street at FamilySearch Catalog.
- West Bromwich: Monumental Inscriptions of Christ Church Graveyard at FamilySearch Catalog.

### Newspaper records

- Darlaston Weekly Times, 1882–1887 at Findmypast — birth, death, and marriage notices.
- British Newspaper Archive (britishnewspaperarchive.co.uk) for wider West Midlands coverage.

### Other records

- Poor rate books, Darlaston, 1893 (FamilySearch volume 008068830_003, 432 images, full-text searchable).
- School records: Staffordshire Record Office; not comprehensively online.
- Probate: England & Wales National Probate Calendar 1858–1995 at Ancestry (collection 1904).
- City/county directories at Ancestry (collection 1547) for year-by-year address location.

## Repository guide

### Online
FamilySearch (free), FreeBMD (free), GRO online (free index), Ancestry (subscription), Findmypast (subscription), Staffordshire BMD / West Midlands BMD (free), FreeReg (free).

### Physical
Staffordshire Record Office, Eastgate Street, Stafford ST16 2LZ — original parish registers, Bishop's Transcripts, Poor Law records, school records.
General Register Office, Southport — original civil registration certificates.
Sandwell Archives — post-1974 local authority records.

## Research tips

- Darlaston births are under Walsall registration district. Search both Walsall and West Bromwich in FreeBMD and GRO.
- Use the GRO website directly for free access to mother's maiden name on birth index entries (not shown on most third-party sites pre-1911).
- Search 1881, 1891, and 1901 censuses for all household members; the 1911 census provides a fertility summary.
- Search burial registers alongside baptism registers — infant name reuse was common.
- Darlaston had four Wesleyan places of worship; search Nonconformist registers if not found in Anglican records.
- Darlaston Weekly Times (1882–1887) may carry infant death notices.
- Check neighbouring parishes Wednesbury and Walsall if not found in Darlaston/West Bromwich registers.
- Staffordshire Name Indexes (staffsnameindexes.org.uk) is a locally-maintained volunteer index worth checking.
